ahmedabad-across-the-sabarmati-1679.jpg.why_this_image: Hero. The walled city seen across the broad, braided Sabarmati bed in 1679, with people and riders fording shallow channels: the founding geography (city on the high east bank, river as a sand bed) in one frame, and the visual answer to the Gazetteer's 'thin stream of water in a broad bed of deep sand'.

Earlier and clearer than any 19th-century photograph of Kankaria found.

pol-gate-2012.jpg.why_this_image: Chapter 4. A pol gate (Gatrad ni Pol, named on its signboard) opening onto a lane of attached houses: the street unit of the old city where the better-off houses kept rain cisterns under their courtyards. No openly licensed photograph of a tanka itself was found on Commons, so the pol street stands in; the caption does not claim a tanka is in frame.

_note:
Source attribution for every image used in the Ahmedabad Origins story. Licence and artist fields were read from the Commons API's extmetadata (LicenseShortName, UsageTerms, Artist, ImageDescription) at download time, not inferred from the file page's rendered HTML. For institutional uploads (Rijksmuseum, British Library) the extmetadata Artist names the institution; the actual maker is taken from the extmetadata ImageDescription and given in `artist` and `credit`. 'No restrictions' is the Commons {{No restrictions}} tag (Flickr Commons institution, no known copyright restrictions). The five CC BY-SA photographs carry the photographer, the licence and the licence URL in the caption next to the image, as well as here. We do not ship images without provenance.

DELIBERATELY NOT USED, having been checked: the 19 candidates under _rejected, each with its reason, so they are not re-fetched. The recurring problems were a Flickr uploader named as the artist of a photograph far older than the account (the 1966 Sabarmati slide), 'Public domain, unknown author' claims resting on a blog with no publication evidence, a 'c.1752' Baldaeus lithograph whose artist died in 1671, mis-dated British Library plates, open-album Rijksmuseum scans with the photograph sideways in a third of the frame, and modern paintings or murals that are not documentary. Thirteen further licence-clean alternates (among them the British Library's 1866 plates of Kankaria's supply sluice and Dada Harir's upper gallery, and Murray's 1903 map) were identified but not downloaded; none is needed by the current text.
